title: Ephemeral Decision Ribbon: lightweight batch+cache recommendations in Console
creator: Aisha Nadeem
description: Problem: Engineers and product teams land in the Console runtime view and need a low-friction way to act on Redwood's batching/cache suggestions without leaving the page. Current recommendation cards are heavy and require multiple navigation steps. Goal: design an ephemeral, top-of-page "Decision Ribbon" that summaries a targeted recommendation (e.g., enable prefix cache + mild batching) with three CTA paths: Apply now, Simulate & Preview, and Explain (microcopy + quick diagram). The ribbon should surface estimated cost delta, expected latency impact, and a safety badge when a recommendation risks model quality. It must be keyboard accessible and collapse into a compact pill on narrow layouts.
design_notes: Keep ribbon visually lightweight (one-line summary + small icon), avoid modal-heavy flows for quick accepts. Use a progressive disclosure pattern: ribbon -> compact detail panel -> full-config editor. Prioritize telemetry hooks (impression, click, apply, simulate) and an API contract for runtime to provide estimated_cost_delta (USD/day), latency_delta_ms, quality_regression_risk (none|low|medium|high). Draft microcopy emphasizes reversibility ("Apply now — can be rolled back in 2 minutes"). Include guardrail states: locked (enterprise-only), blocked (policy/rate-limits), and high-risk (requires PM approval).
acceptance_criteria: Ribbon appears on runtime & per-route model pages when a recommendation exists
CTA: Apply triggers a sandboxed config change that can be rolled back automatically
Simulate opens a side panel showing token-level cost delta and 99th latency projection
Explain shows a 2–3 line rationale + link to full recommendation audit (PRD/drive)
Ribbon passes keyboard focus order and ARIA labeling accessibility checks
Telemetry events logged to analytics: recommendation_shown, recommendation_clicked, recommendation_applied, recommendation_simulated
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false-positive recommendations could reduce quality. Mitigation: show conservative recommendations first and include explicit quality_risk indicator
Risk: ribbon causes alert fatigue. Mitigation: throttle impressions per route and expose dismiss/never-show controls
Risk: telemetry missing for new CTA paths. Mitigation: coordinate with analytics triage doc and instrument before rollout
implementation_notes_for_engineering: Required runtime API fields: recommendation_id, summary_text, estimated_cost_delta_usd_per_day, latency_delta_ms_p50_p95_p99, quality_regression_risk
Server must support apply_preview endpoint that runs simulation without mutating live config
Rollout plan: feature-flag the ribbon per-org with a 10% initial cohort
Design tokens: ribbon background uses console-accent-50; compact pill uses 24px height with 12px horizontal padding
user_flows: 1) User lands on route page -> ribbon shown -> clicks Simulate -> side-panel shows simulated metrics -> user closes
2) User clicks Apply -> confirmation toast + undo snackbar (60s) -> config change recorded in audit log
3) User clicks Explain -> inline microcopy expands + link to full recommendation audit
accessibility_considerations: Ribbon must be reachable as first interactive element landmark on the runtime page
Ensure 4.5:1 contrast for text on ribbon in both standard and compact states
Provide aria-describedby for the quality risk badge and role="status" for simulation completion messages
qa_tasks: Keyboard navigation test across ribbon -> simulate panel -> apply flow
A11y scan for color contrast and screen reader announcements
Integration test for telemetry events recorded end-to-end
recommended_metrics_for_success: No increase in model-quality alerts attributable to applied recommendations in cohort
